haiku-low.q1: It returns 202 with the rejected events (by batch index, plus event_id if present), only after every accepted event is written to the log with all-replica acknowledgement. Malformed events never enter the log.
haiku-low.q2: For 429 the client retries. For 503 it resends the same batch with the same ids. Timeouts and other 5xx responses are NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q3: The copy with the lowest log offset in its log partition for that event_id wins and is loaded into events_clean. Later copies are duplicates, dropped from events_clean but kept in the archive.
haiku-low.q4: Its day is the UTC day of received_at, Tuesday, since client timestamps are never used. It belongs to Tuesday's partition and Tuesday's replay.
haiku-low.q5: In the KV dedup store, keyed by event_id, with value partition:offset. Entries expire automatically after the 8-day TTL.
haiku-low.q6: NOT STATED for unreachable. The plan only says that if the KV store loses data, live ingestion briefly admits duplicates, to be fixed by re-seeding and replay.
haiku-low.q7: Offsets are committed only after progress, so a crash resumes from the last committed offset. The warehouse load is idempotent by event_id, and dedup treats its own partition:offset as the winner, so nothing is lost or double-counted.
haiku-low.q8: Input is the raw envelopes in object storage archive, plus archive indexes and the manifest. Rebuilt rows go to a staging table, then one atomic partition swap puts them into events_clean.
haiku-low.q9: It reads archive indexes for D-8 through D plus the first two hours of D+1. It keeps a copy only if it has the lowest offset for its event_id in its log partition, so any earlier copy, even from an earlier day, causes it to be dropped.
haiku-low.q10: The live partition is left unchanged, since the swap is atomic and any failure stops the job before it. The operator fixes the cause and reruns the replay; a dead job's lock lease expires.
haiku-low.q11: Only closed days, with archive indexes for D-8 through D inside 90-day retention. That is about 82 days; older days are refused.
haiku-low.q12: Not decided. A single bot_policy setting, drop or flag, shared by live and replay, applies after dedup. Bot signals are computed either way, and the archive keeps every event.

sonnet.q1: It checks each event separately and rejects ones missing event_id or device_id or over 32 KB. Rejected events never enter the log. It returns 202 only after all accepted events are written to the log with all-replica acks (acks=all). The 202 lists rejected events by batch index (plus event_id if present).
sonnet.q2: 429: overload, nothing was accepted, client retries. 503: log write failed for the whole batch, client resends the same batch with the same ids; repeats become duplicates and are dropped later. Timeout: NOT STATED explicitly (presumably resend the same batch, since clients resend batches). Clients never retry rejected events.
sonnet.q3: The winner: the copy with the lowest log offset in its log partition for that event_id (all copies share a partition). Others are dropped from events_clean but stay in the archive. Live dedup uses an 8-day window, so a copy arriving after 8 days would be treated as new.
sonnet.q4: Tuesday's UTC day partition and replay. The day comes from the server received_at (00:10 Tuesday), never the client timestamp.
sonnet.q5: In a KV store. Each event gets an atomic set-if-absent on event_id with value partition:offset, and TTL 8 days. Entries are removed by TTL expiry.
sonnet.q6: The plan doesn't say directly what happens during unreachability. It says that if the KV store loses data, live ingestion briefly admits duplicates; fix by re-seeding the last 8 days of keys from archive indexes, then replaying affected days. Collector and archiver are independent of the KV store, and the log (14 days) and archive keep the events.
sonnet.q7: No loss: the processor resumes from its last committed offset, so the batch is reprocessed. No double-counting: the dedup set-if-absent treats a key already holding the event's own partition:offset as the winner, and the warehouse load is idempotent by event_id (merge or insert-if-absent), so the reload adds no duplicates.
sonnet.q8: Input: the raw archive only (envelopes, plus archive indexes and manifest); it never reads the log or the live KV dedup state. Output goes to a staging table (e.g. events_clean_staging_<D>_<run id>), then an atomic single-partition replace swaps it into events_clean.
sonnet.q9: It reads the archive indexes of (event_id, partition, offset) for D-8 through D plus the first two hours of D+1. It keeps a copy stamped D only if it has the lowest offset for its event_id in its log partition; if an earlier copy exists in D or an earlier day, it is dropped. This covers events first received on earlier days.
sonnet.q10: The live partition is untouched (the swap is atomic and happens only after validation and approval), so the warehouse is unchanged. Operator drops the staging table (if one exists), fixes the cause, and reruns. A dead job's lock expires via lease TTL; a failed job releases the lock.
sonnet.q11: Closed days (past 02:00 UTC on D+1 with a closed marker) whose archive manifest exists and matches counts, with indexes for D-8 through D and D-8 within 90-day retention: about the last 82 days. Older days are refused.
sonnet.q12: Undecided. Product hasn't chosen drop vs flag. One setting bot_policy = drop | flag, shared by live and replay, applied after dedup in the enrichment step; bot signals are computed either way; the archive keeps all events. If flag, add a nullable is_suspected_bot column. The bot step must not ship to production until bot_policy has a value. Replay can fix affected days if the decision changes.
